newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-SUPPORT GROWS FOR TEST CRICKET WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SUPPORT GROWS FOR TEST CRICKET WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: England and Pakistan have added their support to a proposal by the editor of the cricketer's bible Wisden to raise the worldwide profile of test cricket.

A blueprint for a world championship of test cricket was unveiled by Wisden's Matthew Engel in October and drew immediate praise from Ali Bacher, managing director of the United Cricket Board of South Africa, who suggested "the time is ripe to take a fresh look at the way tests are organised."

His counterparts in Pakistan and England, Majid Khan and Tim Lamb, have now also endorsed the proposal which Engel believes has "huge potential" for sponsorship. "We are extremely hopeful that the International Cricket Council (ICC) will eventually make the championship official," said Engel. "It would take very little adjustment to the present fixture list and add enormously to cricket's popularity."

If the championship were in operation now, South Africa, Australia and West Indies would be tied in first place, with Australia going clear at the top if they beat West Indies in the third test in Melbourne starting on December 26.

Standings are worked out on the basis of two points for winning a series or one-off test, one point for drawing a series, and none for losing. Only the most recent meetings, home and away, are included. The difference between the number of series played and points gained decides each country's position.
